content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral, especially after recent declines.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; true prices often dip below forecast before rebounding.
- Forecast bias toward higher prices in early horizon (e.g., 1st-3rd day) when sentiment is positive; adjust downward for early periods.
- Mean reversion effect: if forecast is significantly above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5-10% for next 3-5 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2-5% to avoid overcorrection.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment > 0.2 for 3+ days, model overestimates; if sentiment < -0.1, model underestimates — adjust forecast by ±1-3% based on sentiment magnitude.
